transcript_to_article.caption_file_vtt:
WEBVTT

00:00:00.000 --> 00:00:04.000
<v Theo Marsh>Okay, can everyone hear me? Great.

00:00:04.000 --> 00:00:10.000
<v Theo Marsh>Welcome to episode 12 of the Example Booking podcast. Today I'm talking to Rosa Delacourt,

00:00:10.000 --> 00:00:16.000
<v Theo Marsh>who owns Example Hair Studio, about um no-shows and the policy that fixed them.

00:00:16.000 --> 00:00:19.000
<v Rosa Delacourt>Thanks for having me, Theo.

00:00:19.000 --> 00:00:23.000
<v Theo Marsh>So, uh, take me back a year, because I know a lot of people listening are where you were then. Where were you?

00:00:23.000 --> 00:00:30.000
<v Rosa Delacourt>A year ago our no-show rate was 14 percent. You know, that's roughly one empty chair

00:00:30.000 --> 00:00:36.000
<v Rosa Delacourt>out of every seven appointments. We have six stylists, so on a busy Saturday that was

00:00:36.000 --> 00:00:41.000
<v Rosa Delacourt>two or three empty chairs. And the the worst part was color appointments,

00:00:41.000 --> 00:00:46.000
<v Rosa Delacourt>because those block two or three hours of a stylist's day.

00:00:46.000 --> 00:00:48.000
<v Theo Marsh>What did you try first?

00:00:48.000 --> 00:00:55.000
<v Rosa Delacourt>We tried, um, calling every client the day before. It took my front desk about an hour

00:00:55.000 --> 00:00:59.000
<v Rosa Delacourt>every afternoon, and honestly it barely moved the number.

00:00:59.000 --> 00:01:03.000
<v Rosa Delacourt>Half the calls went to voicemail anyway.

00:01:03.000 --> 00:01:05.000
<v Theo Marsh>So what changed?

00:01:05.000 --> 00:01:10.000
<v Rosa Delacourt>We wrote a real no-show policy. I mean, we had one before,

00:01:10.000 --> 00:01:14.000
<v Rosa Delacourt>but it was a line on a sign by the till that nobody read.

00:01:14.000 --> 00:01:21.000
<v Rosa Delacourt>The new one has three parts. First, clients get a text reminder 48 hours before

00:01:21.000 --> 00:01:25.000
<v Rosa Delacourt>the appointment and another one 2 hours before.

00:01:25.000 --> 00:01:32.000
<v Rosa Delacourt>Second, they can cancel or move the booking from that text, up to 24 hours ahead, with no charge.

00:01:32.000 --> 00:01:38.000
<v Rosa Delacourt>And third, for color and anything over two hours, we take a deposit when they book.

00:01:38.000 --> 00:01:41.000
<v Theo Marsh>What does the reminder actually say?

00:01:41.000 --> 00:01:48.000
<v Rosa Delacourt>It's short. Their name, the stylist, the time, and one line that says the deposit

00:01:48.000 --> 00:01:54.000
<v Rosa Delacourt>is kept if they cancel inside 24 hours. Then a link to move or cancel.

00:01:54.000 --> 00:01:59.000
<v Rosa Delacourt>We tried a friendlier, longer version and fewer people tapped the link.

00:01:59.000 --> 00:02:05.000
<v Theo Marsh>Quick word from our sponsor. Example Booking Software sends those reminders for you,

00:02:05.000 --> 00:02:10.000
<v Theo Marsh>and the Starter plan is $19 a month. Okay, back to Rosa.

00:02:10.000 --> 00:02:13.000
<v Theo Marsh>How did clients react to the deposit?

00:02:13.000 --> 00:02:20.000
<v Rosa Delacourt>Like, honestly, I was scared we'd lose people. We didn't, as far as I can tell.

00:02:20.000 --> 00:02:26.000
<v Rosa Delacourt>Two regulars complained in the first month, and both of them still book with us.

00:02:26.000 --> 00:02:33.000
<v Rosa Delacourt>I think the key was that we explained it in person before it ever showed up on a booking.

00:02:33.000 --> 00:02:40.000
<v Rosa Delacourt>Every stylist told their clients at checkout for about three weeks before we switched it on.

00:02:40.000 --> 00:02:44.000
<v Rosa Delacourt>So nobody met the deposit for the first time on a screen.

00:02:44.000 --> 00:02:46.000
<v Theo Marsh>And the numbers?

00:02:46.000 --> 00:02:53.000
<v Rosa Delacourt>After three months the no-show rate was 4 percent. So, uh, from 14 down to 4.

00:02:53.000 --> 00:02:57.000
<v Rosa Delacourt>And the 24-hour window matters as much as the deposit,

00:02:57.000 --> 00:03:02.000
<v Rosa Delacourt>because a cancellation the day before is a slot we can still fill.

00:03:02.000 --> 00:03:04.000
<v Theo Marsh>How do you fill it?

00:03:04.000 --> 00:03:11.000
<v Rosa Delacourt>We keep a waitlist. When someone cancels, the first three people on the list get a text,

00:03:11.000 --> 00:03:14.000
<v Rosa Delacourt>and the first one to reply gets the slot.

00:03:14.000 --> 00:03:20.000
<v Rosa Delacourt>Last month we had 11 late cancellations and the waitlist filled 9 of them.

00:03:20.000 --> 00:03:24.000
<v Theo Marsh>What happens when someone still doesn't show up?

00:03:24.000 --> 00:03:28.000
<v Rosa Delacourt>The first time, we forgive it and we tell them we forgave it.

00:03:28.000 --> 00:03:35.000
<v Rosa Delacourt>The second time, we keep the deposit. Um, we've only had to do that a handful of times,

00:03:35.000 --> 00:03:38.000
<v Rosa Delacourt>and it was always for a color appointment.

00:03:38.000 --> 00:03:42.000
<v Theo Marsh>And your front desk? They were spending an hour a day on calls.

00:03:42.000 --> 00:03:48.000
<v Rosa Delacourt>That's gone. Now it's maybe ten minutes in the morning, checking the waitlist replies.

00:03:48.000 --> 00:03:52.000
<v Rosa Delacourt>They spend that time on the clients who are actually in the building.

00:03:52.000 --> 00:03:56.000
<v Theo Marsh>A lot of owners have told us they're nervous that clients will just go somewhere else. What would you tell a salon that's nervous about charging deposits?

00:03:56.000 --> 00:04:02.000
<v Rosa Delacourt>Start with the appointments that hurt most when they're empty. For us that was color.

00:04:02.000 --> 00:04:08.000
<v Rosa Delacourt>Don't put the fee in the small print. Say it out loud, put it on the booking page,

00:04:08.000 --> 00:04:11.000
<v Rosa Delacourt>and put it in the reminder text.

00:04:11.000 --> 00:04:17.000
<v Rosa Delacourt>And, you know, make cancelling easy. If moving a booking takes one tap,

00:04:17.000 --> 00:04:21.000
<v Rosa Delacourt>people move it instead of just not showing up.

00:04:21.000 --> 00:04:24.000
<v Theo Marsh>Would you ever drop the deposit?

00:04:24.000 --> 00:04:31.000
<v Rosa Delacourt>Not for color. For a quick trim, I think it probably costs more goodwill than it saves.

00:04:31.000 --> 00:04:36.000
<v Rosa Delacourt>We don't take one for trims, and our trim no-shows are low anyway.

00:04:36.000 --> 00:04:40.000
<v Theo Marsh>Last thing before we go. How long have you had the studio?

00:04:40.000 --> 00:04:46.000
<v Rosa Delacourt>Eight years this spring. I started with two chairs in a room above a bakery,

00:04:46.000 --> 00:04:51.000
<v Rosa Delacourt>and we moved to the current place when we hired our fourth stylist.

00:04:51.000 --> 00:04:56.000
<v Rosa Delacourt>The bakery is still there, and I still miss the smell of it every morning.

00:04:56.000 --> 00:05:02.000
<v Rosa Delacourt>My very first client from those days still comes in for a cut every six weeks.

00:05:02.000 --> 00:05:05.000
<v Theo Marsh>That's loyalty. Where can people find you?

00:05:05.000 --> 00:05:10.000
<v Rosa Delacourt>We're on Main Street, and the booking page is linked from our Instagram.

00:05:10.000 --> 00:05:13.000
<v Theo Marsh>Rosa, this was great. Thanks for coming on.

00:05:13.000 --> 00:05:16.000
<v Rosa Delacourt>Thanks, Theo, this was fun.
